name: Dhaulagiri I Expedition
sub_region: Myagdi District, Gandaki Province (approach also via Mustang/Kali Gandaki)

difficulty.notes: 8,167 m, 7th highest mountain. Normal route is the Northeast Ridge (Swiss-Austrian first ascent, 13 May 1960). Glacier below the 'Eiger' rock face and the Dhaulagiri icefall to the NE col; steep fixed-rope sections Camp 1-Camp 2; wind-exposed ridge to Camp 3; avalanche-prone east-side slabs if Camp 2 is pitched off the ridge. Operators require prior 6,000-7,000 m experience. [s3][s4][s5][s6]

duration_days.notes: Common approach: drive Pokhara-Marpha, trek via Yak Kharka and Dhampus (Thapa) Pass (~5,244-5,250 m) and Hidden Valley to Base Camp (4,700-4,750 m). Alternative spring approach from Beni up the Myagdi Khola via Darbang and Italian Base Camp (3,660 m) and the Chhonbardan Glacier. Helicopter access to BC is used by some teams. [s3][s4][s7]

itinerary.route: Acclimatisation day in Marpha (optional Muktinath excursion)
Yak Kharka - Dhampus/Thapa Pass (~5,244 m) - Hidden Valley (Dhampus Base Camp)
Hidden Valley - French Pass (~5,360 m) - Dhaulagiri Base Camp
Acclimatisation and rotations: BC - Camp I (5,850-5,900 m) - Camp II (6,400-6,600 m) - touch Camp III - BC
itinerary.notes: C1 on the NE col after glacier/icefall; C1-C2 is the most technical stage per SST with steep ice and ladders. Advance BC (~5,300 m) used only as a gear depot due to avalanche danger. [s3][s4][s5]

itinerary.route: Summit window: BC - Camp II - Camp III (7,200-7,400 m) - summit (8,167 m) - descend to C2/BC
itinerary.notes: Late-night start; summit typically 8-10 am; oxygen used by commercial teams. [s3][s5][s6]

best_seasons.notes: Spring easier on the lower glacier (snow-covered crevasses); autumn has more open crevasses and rock below the 'Eiger'. [s5] Operators describe Myagdi approach in spring and Marpha/Hidden Valley approach in autumn. [s4]

permits.name: Mountaineering royalty (Department of Tourism) - peaks above 8,000 m except Everest and Manaslu
permits.fee: Per foreign climber: USD 3,000 spring, USD 1,500 autumn, USD 750 winter/summer

permits.name: Garbage management deposit (peaks above 8,000 m)
permits.fee: USD 3,000 per expedition, refundable on compliance

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) - for Marpha/Hidden Valley approach through ACA
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per foreign national (SAARC NPR 1,000), tax included

guide_requirements: Sixth amendment to the Mountaineering Regulations bars solo ascents of 8,000 m peaks; at least one high-altitude worker or mountain guide per two members. [s2][s9] Government-deputed liaison officer required for expedition teams under the Tourism Act. [s10]

flights: Optional Jomsom - Pokhara ~20-25 min on return [s4][s11]
Helicopter to/from Base Camp used by some teams [s6]
drives: Pokhara - Beni - Marpha via Kali Gandaki road [s3]
Alternative: Pokhara - Beni - Darbang for Myagdi approach [s4]
logistics.notes: Lodges to Marpha; camping from Yak Kharka; ~1 month at tented Base Camp with helicopter resupply. [s3]

highlights: Approach over Dhampus Pass and French Pass via Hidden Valley [s3][s7]
Views across the Kali Gandaki gorge to Annapurna I [s12]
risks: Crevasses and icefall below the NE col, worse in autumn [s5]
Avalanche-prone wind slabs on the east side near Camp 2 [s5]
Strong wind on the upper ridge before Camp 3 [s4]
High passes (5,200-5,360 m) on the approach before acclimatisation [s3]

acclimatization.notes: Rotation period roughly days 9-27 in the commercial programme. [s3]

unverified: Hidden Valley overnight altitude not consistently published.
Yak Kharka altitude: SST outbound day lists 4,900 m but return day and another operator list 3,680 m (3,680 m used).
ACAP applicability for the expedition approach via Marpha/Hidden Valley (route passes through Mustang inside ACA, but not confirmed from an official expedition source).
Permit validity reported shortened from 75 to 55 days in the 2025 amendment (confirmed for Everest reporting only).
